football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.5 points.
supporting: When Clemson has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Clemson’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.1% of its dropbacks, and Syracuse’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When Clemson has the ball (the red zone): Clemson’s offense succeeds on 30.4% of its red-zone plays, and Syracuse’s defense allows success on 44.7% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).

When Clemson has the ball (big plays through the air): Clemson’s offense turns 7.6% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Syracuse’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Clemson has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Clemson’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 20.2% of its runs, and Syracuse’s defense stops 21.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
contradicting: When Syracuse has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Syracuse’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.9% of its dropbacks, and Clemson’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Syracuse has the ball (big plays through the air): Syracuse’s offense turns 10.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Clemson’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.9% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
